LH-REG-002.question: An insurer incorporated in Bermuda wants to sell life insurance policies to residents of New Jersey. In New Jersey, this company is classified as:
LH-REG-002.explanation: Under N.J.S.A. 17B:17-7, an alien insurer is formed under the laws of a country other than the United States. A foreign insurer is formed in a different U.S. state, which is the tempting choice but applies only to companies formed within the United States.

LH-REG-003.question: An insurer incorporated in Ohio has received a certificate of authority from New Jersey and sells policies there. In New Jersey, it is considered:
LH-REG-003.explanation: Under N.J.S.A. 17B:17-7 and 17B:17-11, a company formed in another state is foreign, and one holding a current certificate of authority is admitted (authorized). Non-admitted would apply only if it lacked a certificate, and it is domestic only in Ohio.

LH-PROV-004.explanation: New Jersey requires a grace period of 30 days, or one month of at least 30 days (N.J.S.A. 17B:25-3), so the policy was still in force on March 20. The insurer pays the face amount minus the overdue premium: $100,000 - $1,200 = $98,800, not the full $100,000.
